passages.section: Section 0. What the agent starts with
passages.text: Section 0. What the agent starts with. Every transaction carries a `risk_score` between 0 and 1 from the bank's detection model. The model is useful and imperfect: many high scores are legitimate, and some fraud scores low. A score is a reason to look, never a verdict. The only confirmed outcomes are in the closed cases.

Controls should ensure limited access to the monitoring systems, and changes should generally require the approval of the BSA compliance officer or senior management. Management should document and be able to explain filtering criteria, thresholds used, and how both are appropriate for the bank's risks. Management should also periodically review and test the filtering criteria and thresholds established to ensure that they are still effective. In addition, the monitoring system's programming methodology and effectiveness should be independently validated to ensure that the models are detecting potentially suspicious activity. The independent validation should also verify the policies in place and that management is complying with those policies. Managing Alerts Alert management focuses on processes used to investigate and evaluate identified unusual activity. assessment.reasoning: Transaction 3640919 was flagged solely by the legacy real-time risk score (0.71) for an $881.55 in-person purchase of product W in region 494. However, the bank's calibrated second-generation fraud model scored this transaction at only 0.003, with an empirical historical fraud rate of 0.0063 (0.63%), indicating that the legacy score is an uncorroborated false alarm. The transaction was conducted in person with no device anomalies, no card testing sequence, and no customer dispute. Furthermore, region 494 is not new for card C09241-K2: the card has 491 historical transactions in this region and recorded 6 in-person transactions there over the preceding 10 days, while the shared origin analysis shows zero transactions scoring above 0.5 (lift 0.0 vs base rate). Although card C09241-K2 has historical closed fraud cases from September and October 2016, holder C09241-K2|494|-43 has zero prior transactions associated with confirmed fraud, and the card is not part of any active fraud ring (ring_id -1). All six most similar closed cases involving model alerts on large transactions were cleared as legitimate cardholder purchases. The evidence indicates this alert is a false alarm and the activity is legitimate.
